standard_prerequisites.name: Reduction of a comparison of sites to a comparison of small categories and coverings
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Topologies, Lemma topologies-lemma-contained-in (022J) and Lemma topologies-lemma-alternative (04HR), plus Sets, Lemma sets-lemma-what-is-in-it (000R); invoked at proof lines 2138, 2140 and 2149
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the reduction to the case of nested big sites, the smallness fact that every affine scheme etale over S sits in both, and the criterion that an equivalence preserving standard coverings induces an equivalence of topoi.

core_obligations: Reduce to nested universes: given two big etale sites Sch_etale and Sch_etale' containing S, one may assume Sch_etale contained in Sch_etale', so that the two constructions of the small site sit inside one another (proof lines 2135-2139).

Show the small categories agree: every affine scheme etale over S is isomorphic to an object of both big sites, so the induced functor S_{affine, etale} -> S'_{affine, etale} is an equivalence of categories (proof lines 2140-2145).

Show coverings are preserved: both that functor and a quasi-inverse send standard etale coverings to standard etale coverings, so the criterion for comparing topologies applies and the two topoi are canonically equivalent, which proves the independence from the universe (proof lines 2145-2149).
proof_roadmap: Put the two big sites in a nested position using the comparison lemma for sites (proof lines 2135-2139).
Use the smallness statement about sets of schemes to see that the small etale sites have the same objects up to isomorphism, hence the induced functor is an equivalence (proof lines 2140-2145).
Check that standard coverings correspond on both sides and invoke the criterion for equivalence of topologies (proof lines 2145-2149).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the etale topos of a scheme S is determined up to canonical equivalence by S alone, independently of the construction of the small etale site inside a chosen partial universe (statement lines 2129-2131). The proof has to separate two different kinds of input: a set-theoretic one, that every affine scheme etale over S is isomorphic to an object of both big sites so that the two small categories are equivalent, and a topological one, that this equivalence and a quasi-inverse preserve standard etale coverings (proof lines 2140-2149). Only after both are in place does the criterion for comparing topologies apply. The claim is H2: a short but genuinely two-ingredient comparison.
